evidence: createApp/productRoutes/orderRoutes only set up routes and call application services (catalogue.addProduct, orders.placeOrder, orders.transition).
requireString/requireNumber/asObject/param only check that request input is well-formed, which is normal adapter work.
statusFor and errorHandler turn DomainError subclasses into HTTP status codes. This is transport-layer error translation.
The ACTIONS map links URL action names to OrderState values. Whether a transition is valid is still decided by orders.transition (application/domain).
The query and body state checks call the domain's isOrderState instead of copying the domain rule into this file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http.ts is an HTTP transport adapter. Its jobs are building the Express app, defining routes, checking the shape of request bodies (asObject, requireString, requireNumber, param), turning domain errors into HTTP status codes (statusFor, errorHandler) and building JSON responses. All of these are transport concerns that fit an infrastructure layer. Every business operation is handed off to CatalogueService and OrderService: placeOrder, transition, listOrders, addProduct. The file does not decide which state transitions are valid or whether there is enough stock. It does not compute prices or persist anything. The ACTIONS map turns URL action words into target states. That is a routing alias, not a business rule, because the domain still checks whether the transition is valid. The state check calls the domain's own isOrderState and ORDER_STATES rather than repeating the rule here. No ADR prose was provided to check against.
